messages.text: Hey team, following up on yesterday's meeting. I've been thinking about the sharding strategy for the user table. We're approaching 500M rows and queries are slowing down.
We should shard by user_id range. Geographic sharding would be cleaner but our user distribution is too skewed.
Agree with @Priya. Hash-based sharding on user_id gives us even distribution. We can use Vitess as the proxy layer.
OK, we'll go with hash-based sharding using Vitess. @James can you set up a Vitess PoC environment by next Wednesday?
On it. I'll have the Vitess PoC running on staging by Wednesday Sept 3rd.
We also need to update the data access layer. I'll refactor the repository pattern to support shard-aware queries. Should take about a week.
Great. Let's sync next Thursday to review the PoC results. This is a big change — we should get Sarah's sign-off before proceeding to production.
Proposal: migrate the order service from CRUD to event sourcing. Current issues: audit trail is incomplete, we can't replay state, and debugging production issues is painful.
Event sourcing is a big architectural shift. What's the estimated effort?
About 3 sprints for the core event store, then 2 more for migrating existing orders. We'd use Kafka as the event bus.
I like this. The decision is to adopt event sourcing for the order service using Kafka. Priya, can you write up the technical design doc by September 5th?
Will do. I'll include the migration strategy and rollback plan.
Make sure to consider GDPR implications — event stores make data deletion harder. We need a strategy for handling deletion requests.
Good catch. I'll add a crypto-shredding approach for GDPR compliance in the design doc.
We need to standardize our state management. Currently we have Redux in 3 apps, MobX in 2, and plain React context in 4. This is unsustainable.
I've evaluated options. Zustand is the most lightweight and has the best DX. It's also compatible with our SSR setup.
From a design system perspective, we should use Zustand. It integrates well with our component architecture.
Let's go with Zustand as our standard state management solution. @Nina, can you create a migration playbook by September 8th? Include examples for converting from Redux and MobX.
Sure thing. I'll also set up an eslint rule to flag new Redux/MobX usage.
Our k8s clusters are running 1.27, which goes EOL in October. We need to upgrade to 1.29.
We should upgrade to 1.29 — it has the KEP for sidecar containers which we need for the service mesh.
Agreed. The plan is to upgrade staging first, then production with a 1-week bake time. @Lisa, can you handle the staging upgrade by September 10th?
Yes. I'll do staging first. Production upgrade should happen during our next maintenance window on September 20th.
We also need to update all Helm charts for compatibility. Someone from each team needs to test their services on staging after the upgrade.
Quick thread: we currently use URL-based API versioning (/v1/, /v2/) but it's causing routing complexity. Proposal to switch to header-based versioning.
Header-based is harder for frontend to debug. Can we use a hybrid — URL for major versions, headers for minor?
I like the hybrid approach. It keeps things debuggable while reducing route duplication.

OK, we agreed on hybrid API versioning: URL path for major versions, Accept-Version header for minor versions. I'll update the API standards doc. @Priya, can you implement this in the API gateway by September 12th?
Will do. I'll also add gateway middleware to handle the version negotiation.
